jobs.title: Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description
Taha Tech Solutions is a results-driven digital agency specializing in B2B lead generation, graphic design, and performance marketing. The company helps businesses grow by delivering high-quality leads, compelling visual content, and data-driven advertising strategies. With a clear focus on “design better, market smarter, and scale faster,” Taha Tech Solutions partners closely with clients to align creative and marketing efforts with business goals. Team members work in a fast-paced, outcome-oriented environment where innovation, analytics, and collaboration drive success.
Role Description
The Chief Information Officer (CIO) is a full-time, remote role responsible for overseeing the overall information technology vision, strategy, and operations at Taha Tech Solutions. This role involves leading the IT function to support digital agency services, including managing infrastructure, systems, security, and data governance. The CIO will collaborate with executive leadership to align IT strategy with business objectives, optimize business processes, and ensure technology solutions are scalable, reliable, and cost-effective. Day-to-day tasks include directing IT teams, prioritizing projects, implementing best practices in IT management, monitoring performance and risk, and driving continuous improvement in systems and workflows. The CIO will also evaluate emerging technologies, manage vendor relationships, and ensure compliance with relevant standards and regulations.
Qualifications

Candidates should possess strong skills in Information Technology and IT Operations to manage infrastructure, systems, and security effectively.
Candidates should possess skills in IT Management to lead teams, oversee projects, and maintain high service levels.
Candidates should possess skills in IT Strategy and Business Process to align technology initiatives with organizational goals and optimize workflows.
Proven experience in a senior IT leadership role, preferably as CIO, CTO, or equivalent in a digital, marketing, or technology-focused organization.
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute long-term technology roadmaps and transformation initiatives.
Strong understanding of cloud-based solutions, data analytics, cybersecurity practices, and enterprise software platforms.
Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, with the ability to collaborate across technical and non-technical teams.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree or relevant certifications (e.g., ITIL, PMP, CISSP) are beneficial.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology Consultant
jobs.description:
Director of Information Technology Consultant

Location: West Central Texas
Employment Type: Interim / Consulting Assignment
Duration: Approximately 3–6 months
Pay Rate: Approximately $125/hour, subject to final engagement structure
Work Arrangement: Onsite Monday–Thursday; approved temporary housing and travel expenses reimbursed

Position Overview

A public-sector organization in Texas is seeking an experienced Consultant - Director of Information Technology to provide executive leadership and operational continuity during a period of technology transformation.

This individual will lead enterprise technology operations while helping the organization strengthen service delivery, accountability, governance, cybersecurity, infrastructure, applications, and overall technology operations. The Interim Director will work closely with executive leadership, department leaders, technical teams, consultants, and service providers.

The ideal candidate is an experienced IT executive who can quickly assess an organization, establish priorities, stabilize operations, develop staff, manage risk, and advance an existing technology transformation roadmap while maintaining reliable day-to-day services.

Key Responsibilities

Provide executive leadership and accountability for enterprise IT operations and services.
Maintain continuity and reliability of critical technology services across a complex 24/7 operating environment.
Establish clear service ownership, accountability, performance expectations, escalation procedures, documentation, and backup coverage.
Assess organizational capabilities, staffing needs, service gaps, and operational priorities.
Coach and develop technology staff while utilizing vendors, consultants, and managed service providers as appropriate.
Strengthen IT service management practices across incidents, requests, problems, changes, service levels, knowledge management, assets, and continual improvement.
Partner with executive and departmental leadership to communicate technology risks, priorities, resource requirements, investments, and service performance.
Strengthen technology governance, project prioritization, architecture, cybersecurity, change management, and reporting processes.
Maintain and advance technology roadmaps and project portfolios while balancing operational demands, technical debt, cybersecurity, lifecycle requirements, and available resources.
Provide oversight across enterprise applications, data, integrations, automation, infrastructure, cloud platforms, networks, identity, endpoints, and workplace technology.
Support mission-critical and regulated technology environments, including public safety, emergency communications, operational technology, and other essential services.
Oversee cybersecurity, technology risk, incident response, resilience, recovery, and applicable compliance requirements.
Manage technology vendors, contracts, managed services, licensing, renewals, service levels, and deliverables.
Oversee technology budgets, investments, staffing requirements, and lifecycle planning.
Advance an established technology transformation roadmap and prepare the organization for a successful transition to permanent leadership.

Qualifications

Significant leadership experience within enterprise information technology.
Experience leading professional and technical teams, technology operations, budgets, vendors, and complex services.
Demonstrated success stabilizing technology operations and leading organizational or technology transformation.
Strong understanding of cybersecurity, resilience, infrastructure/cloud services, enterprise applications, data, service management, governance, enterprise architecture, and vendor management.
Experience supporting regulated, mission-critical, public safety, critical infrastructure, utility, government, or comparable 24/7 environments.
Experience with CJIS or comparable security and compliance environments is highly desirable.
Strong executive communication, decision-making, staff development, relationship management, financial management, and change leadership skills.
Bachelor's degree in a related discipline preferred; equivalent executive technology experience may be considered.
ITIL, PMP, CGCIO, CISSP, CISM, CRISC, COBIT, or similar certifications are desirable.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a seasoned technology executive who is comfortable stepping into a complex organization, quickly establishing credibility, evaluating immediate priorities, and leading through change. Previous CIO, IT Director, Deputy CIO, Assistant IT Director, or comparable enterprise technology leadership experience within government, utilities, public safety, critical infrastructure, or another complex 24/7 environment would translate particularly well.

Please submit your resume in Word or PDF format to be considered.

15 years of experience in software engineering, with 8 years in a technical engineering role.
10 years of experience in engineering leadership.

Preferred qualifications:

Experience building technical strategy and roadmaps with customer requirements in a dynamic environment.
Ability to build alignment with partner infrastructure teams to execute collaboratively.
Ability to distill complex technical and organizational challenges into clear, actionable narratives for senior leadership and partners.
Proven track record of leading large engineering organizations (50+ people) in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.
Proven success in building collaborative and high-accountability team cultures that attract talent.

About The Job

As the Engineering Director for the Product Experimentation and Evaluations team, you will lead the transformation of Google's product testing and market impact assessment ecosystem for the AI era. You will develop and implement a strategy that shifts from fragmented, human-led analytics and experimentation platforms toward an integrated, agent-centric ecosystem optimized to rapidly provide trusted market insights. This will involve leveraging AI and agents to streamline experiment configuration, eliminate human toil, and guarantee the integrity of evaluation analysis.

Agentic development dramatically reduces the cost of feature implementation, resulting in market leadership being determined by the speed at which we are able to extract reliable insights from concurrent experiments. This role provides the opportunity to radically transform Google’s ability to ship the most impactful products.

The Core team builds the technical foundation behind Google’s flagship products. We are owners and advocates for the underlying design elements, developer platforms, product components, and infrastructure at Google. These are the essential building blocks for excellent, safe, and coherent experiences for our users and drive the pace of innovation for every developer. We look across Google’s products to build central solutions, break down technical barriers and strengthen existing systems. As the Core team, we have a mandate and a unique opportunity to impact important technical decisions across the company.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $307000 - $427000 (USD) + 30% bonus target + equity + benefits

Responsibilities

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Define strategy and lead consolidation of disparate experimentation tools/teams into a single, cohesive platform that delivers on needs of product areas to innovate, experiment, evaluate, and ship at massive scale/speed. Drive rapid execution of the platform strategy, with focus on accelerating product area success in evaluating features in the market and generating trustworthy insights with full agentic execution of the experimentation lifecycle.
Navigate highly-volatile and fast-evolving product requirements as AI-native capabilities continue to transform both user-facing features and internal developer workflows.
Manage/build a team with a culture of technical excellence, customer obsession, partnership, and bias-to-action.
Work with cross-functional leaders to achieve alignment on strategy roadmaps, drive coordinated execution against strategic goals, and ensure success for our customers.
Optimize roadmap execution and adapt priorities to balance near-term customer needs with long-term strategic outcomes.

jobs.description:
*To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.*

Job Category


Program \& Project Management
Job Details


**About Salesforce**

Salesforce is the \#1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.


Ready to level\-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.


**The Experience**
------------------

  

We are seeking an exceptional Senior Director of Technology Program Management to serve as the execution backbone for the Chief Data Officer’s organization. This leader will own portfolio governance and execution across our most strategic Data/AI ML Platforms, Analytics, AI, Integration, Automation, Governance, and platform transformation initiatives. The role requires a rare combination of deep technical fluency, exceptional program rigor, executive presence, and the courage to drive accountability across organizational boundaries.


This is not a traditional PMO role. We are looking for a technology leader who can operate at executive altitude while going deep enough to understand architecture, data flows, technical dependencies, product constraints, operational readiness, and delivery risk. This person will create clarity where there is ambiguity, surface issues early, drive decisions, and ensure that commitments translate into measurable outcomes.  



  

**What You’ll Actually Be Doing**

  

**Portfolio Strategy \& Governance**

  

* Own the end\-to\-end portfolio operating model for the Chief Data \& Intelligence Office, connecting strategy, investments, roadmaps, milestones, dependencies, capacity, risks, and measurable business outcomes.
* Establish a single, trusted view of portfolio health: what is on track, what is at risk, why it is at risk, who owns recovery, and what decisions or executive interventions are required.
* Drive annual and quarterly planning, prioritization, sequencing, resource trade\-offs, portfolio reviews, and executive steering mechanisms across a highly interdependent technology landscape.
Define portfolio health metrics and mechanisms that improve delivery predictability, decision velocity, dependency management, and value realization.  
* 

  

**Technical Program Leadership**

  

* Lead large\-scale, technically complex Data \& AI programs spanning modern data platforms, data engineering and ingestion, analytics, governance, master/reference data, integration and APIs, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, generative AI, agents, and enterprise automation.
* Partner deeply with Product, Engineering, Architecture, Security, Operations, Governance, and business leaders to translate technical roadmaps into executable integrated plans.
* Understand and challenge architecture, sequencing, non\-functional requirements, technical debt, security, reliability, scalability, data quality, and production\-readiness assumptions; identify systemic risks before they become delivery failures.
Manage critical cross\-program and cross\-platform dependencies, including dependencies across Data Solutions, other Digital Enterprise Technology pillars, Technology \& Product, business teams, and strategic partners.  
* 

  

**Execution Excellence \& Accountability**

  

* Create a culture where commitments mean something. Establish clear owners, dates, decision rights, exit criteria, and measurable outcomes—and hold yourself and others equally accountable.
* Surface risks and uncomfortable truths early. Constructively call out missed commitments, insufficient ownership, slow decisions, or execution gaps, and drive a credible recovery plan.
* Lead high\-cadence operating reviews and technical deep dives that remove blockers, accelerate decisions, and keep business\-critical milestones on track.
Balance inclusion with accountability: invite diverse perspectives, build trust, and create psychological safety while maintaining a high bar for performance, transparency, and follow\-through.  
* 

  

**Cross\-Organizational Leadership**

  

* Influence without authority across senior leaders and globally distributed teams; resolve competing priorities and drive alignment when ownership spans multiple organizations.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to VP/SVP executives, translating complex technical and execution signals into concise insights, choices, risks, and recommendations.
Reduce organizational friction by clarifying ownership, resolving dependency conflicts, and ensuring teams understand how their commitments affect the broader portfolio.  
* 

  

**AI\-First Leadership**

  

* Be a visible role model for AI\-first ways of working. Personally use AI and automation to improve planning, synthesis, dependency analysis, risk detection, executive reporting, decision support, and program operations.
* Bring practical fluency in generative AI, LLMs, agents, agentic workflows, RAG, embeddings/vector search, context engineering, tool orchestration, evaluation, observability, AI governance, and responsible AI.
* Challenge the TPM organization to automate coordination work, codify reusable AI skills and workflows, and demonstrate measurable gains in speed, quality, and capacity.
Partner with technical teams to ensure AI programs are grounded in trusted data, governed context, secure access, measurable quality, and production\-grade operational controls.  
* 

  

**Team Leadership \& Culture**

  

* Build, mentor, and scale a high\-performing portfolio and Technical Program Management organization; develop leaders

jobs.title: Director of Technology
jobs.description:
**Department:** Technology
  
**Reports to:** Executive Leadership
  
**Location:** Remote (with some on\-site presence at PA facilities)
  
**Type:** Full\-time
  
**Direct Reports:** Information Technology Lead, External vendors and contractors
  
  

About Gordon Sinclair
  
  

Gordon Sinclair is a promotional products supplier and manufacturer with over 35 years of experience bringing award\-winning branded merchandise to market for some of the most recognized companies in the world. We design, source, and produce a curated line of premium lifestyle products: items built to carry a brand, not just a logo.
  
  

The Role
  
  

Gordon Sinclair is looking for its first dedicated technology leader to maximize the return on technology investment. This role will connect technology to business strategy, establish governance across systems and vendors, coordinate work across functions, build the technology team, and ensure it has the processes, priorities, and support to deliver.
  
  

This is not a maintenance role. This is a leadership role. You will own the technology strategy, the vendor relationships, the roadmap, and the cross\-functional coordination. You will manage an existing IT Director and work alongside operational leaders across Sales, Operations, Product Development, and Supply Chain. You will sit on the leadership team with the authority to drive change across the organization.
  
  

The right candidate is someone who builds strong foundations. The first six months are about understanding what exists, documenting, introducing governance, and building trust across the business. You are here to make what exists work, evaluate what should change, and build a roadmap grounded in business outcomes.
  
  

Core Responsibilities
  
  

Technology Strategy and Roadmap
  
  

* Own the technology strategy and create a prioritized 12\-month roadmap aligned to revenue growth and margin improvement goals.
* Evaluate whether current platform decisions are right\-sized for Gordon Sinclair, and recommend changes where justified by usage, cost, and strategic fit.
* Translate business priorities into technology investment decisions and ensure leadership understands the trade\-offs.


Governance and Risk Management
  
  

* Introduce source control, code review, change control, and testing practices across all custom development.
* Implement monitoring and alerting across the integration layer so failures are detected in real time, not after the fact.
* Maintain a dependency map of production scripts, integrations, and data structures to prevent cascading failures during system changes.
* Maintain an infrastructure registry documenting every system, where it lives, who built it, and how to access it.
* Ensure that work done by contractors and IT personnel is documented, and that the company retains full knowledge of what was built.


Vendor and Contractor Management
  
  

* Own all technology vendor relationships with documented scope, deliverables, spend tracking, and accountability.
* Evaluate vendor performance and make build\-vs\-buy recommendations based on business need, not familiarity.
* Assess whether industry\-focused middleware should be retained or brought in\-house to enable greater cost effectiveness, control, and scalability.


Cross\-Functional Process Ownership
  
  

* Implement workflow and project management tooling so that cross\-functional processes live in systems that enforce accountability.
* Bridge the communication gap between technology and business functions by establishing a standing reporting cadence that translates technology work into business language.


Visibility and Reporting
  
  

* Provide leadership with visibility into backlogged work, work in progress, and delivered outcomes.
* Visualize the pipeline of technology work and its business value so investment decisions are grounded in outcomes, not assumptions.
* Identify key points of failure in existing technology and plan remediation proactively, before they become emergencies.
* Track and report on technology’s contribution to business outcomes, including integration success rates, time\-to\-market for new products, and data completeness.


Team Leadership
  
  

* Manage the IT Lead, providing prioritization, direction, and a structured reporting cadence.
* Evaluate staffing needs and make the case for supplemental resources where the workload exceeds capacity.
* Establish cross\-training and documentation practices to reduce key\-person risk.


Industry Integration
  
  

* Assess PromoStandards compliance gaps and create a prioritized implementation plan to support distributor growth and automated order flow.
* Ensure the distributor\-facing technology quality matches the quality of Gordon Sinclair’s products.


Security and Policy
  
  

* Own IT and InfoSec policies surrounding the usage of technology at Gordon Sinclair, including AI.
* Coordinate with managed service providers on ITSM and infrastructure, with clear division of responsibilities.


Required Qualifications
  
  

* 7\+ years in technology leadership roles with direct responsibility for strategy, vendor management, budgets, and cross\-functional coordination.
* Experience with ERP platforms (NetSuite strongly preferred) in a manufacturing or distribution environment.
* Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into technology roadmaps and communicate technology outcomes to non\-technical leadership.
* Experience introducing governance practices (change control, source control, code review, monitoring) into growing organizations.
* Experience managing vendor and contractor relationships with accountability for scope, deliverables, and spend.
* Experience managing and developing technical staff.
* Experience managing offshore technical resources.


Preferred Qualifications
  
  

* Experience in the promotional products industry or adjacent B2B distribution/manufacturing sectors.
* Familiarity with PromoStandards,

jobs.title: Compliance Program Manager
jobs.description:
Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.


By combining comprehensive commerce\-enablement technology with high\-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator\-built software suite including OMS, Pre\- and Post\-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.


With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end\-to\-end commerce solutions combine best\-in\-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.


Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry\-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top\-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.


Role Overview
  

The Program Manager, Compliance is a strategic driver of Stord’s operational strength and commercial growth. This role is responsible for scaling enterprise compliance programs across OSHA, EPA, GMP, and adjacent regulatory regimes \- building the infrastructure that enables Stord to operate with confidence, win in the market, and deliver on the compliance commitments that today’s leading brands require from a fulfillment partner. A mature, well\-run compliance program is not just a risk management function at Stord; it is a competitive differentiator that unlocks customer revenue, supports network expansion, and protects the business at scale.
  

  

Reporting to the Director of Health, Safety \& Security, this is an enterprise\-level, network\-wide role that operates at the intersection of compliance, operations, and growth. The Program Manager partners closely with Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and Finance to ensure compliance capabilities are a strength Stord leads with \- enabling the business to pursue regulated customer segments, scale into new markets, and demonstrate the program maturity that top\-tier brands demand. The work product of this role is what the entire organization is built around: scalable written programs, audit frameworks, certification standards, reporting infrastructure, and regulatory intelligence systems that grow stronger as Stord grows.
**What This Role Owns**
=======================

This role owns the enterprise compliance program architecture \- the standards, written programs, audit frameworks, and governance mechanisms that define what ‘compliant’ looks like at every Stord facility. The work product of this role is what the rest of the organization is held accountable to. Specifically:


* Enterprise compliance program design, construction, and ownership across OSHA, EPA, GMP, GDP, DOT, and applicable state and local regulatory frameworks \- building programs from the ground up where gaps exist and elevating inconsistent standards to enterprise\-grade.
* Regulatory intelligence: continuously monitoring rulemaking, agency guidance, and enforcement trends; converting regulatory change into updated enterprise programs before gaps become violations.
* Enterprise audit and inspection framework: designing the internal audit program architecture, defining scope and methodology, and building the tools and cadences that keep the network inspection\-ready \- not conducting site audits, but building the system that governs them.
* Enterprise compliance documentation infrastructure: designing and owning the system of record for all written programs, SOPs, training requirements, certifications, and regulatory correspondence \- the single source of truth for compliance across the network.
* Customer and industry certification programs: GMP, GDP, CTPAT, TAPA, and other regulated operating standards required by Stord’s customer base.
* Regulatory agency relationships: serving as the primary compliance point of contact for OSHA, EPA, and other agencies at the program level.
* Enterprise compliance reporting, data, and dashboards: building the metrics infrastructure that gives the Head of HSS, senior leadership, and the broader business real\-time visibility into compliance performance, risk posture, and program health across the network.
* Enterprise compliance training architecture: defining what training is required, for whom, at what frequency, and in what format \- building the content and governance framework that regional and site teams deliver against.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

**OSHA Compliance Program Management**
--------------------------------------

* Build and own Stord’s enterprise OSHA compliance program \- designing the written program architecture, establishing network\-wide standards, and creating the governance mechanisms that ensure consistent compliance across every facility regardless of size, volume, or operational complexity.
* Maintain and update OSHA\-required written programs: Hazard Communication, Lockout/Tagout, Respiratory Protection, Emergency Action Plans, Powered Industrial Truck programs, and others as applicable.
* Oversee OSHA recordkeeping standards across the network \- establishing recordkeeping protocols, auditing site\-level logs for accuracy, and managing 300A

jobs.title: MKE Program Manager
jobs.description:
Covenant Aviation Security (CAS) is seeking an experienced Program Manager to lead airport security operations at Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport (MKE). This position is accountable for ensuring security operations meet contractual requirements, client expectations, regulatory standards, and company policies and procedures. The Program Manager provides direct oversight of operational performance and workforce management, including staffing, scheduling, training, badging, employee performance, compliance, and administrative functions. The position also serves as a key liaison between CAS and airport, regulatory, law enforcement, and other external stakeholders.
  
Company History
  
Founded in 2002, Covenant Aviation Security (CAS) was established to provide a higher standard of transportation security following the events of September 11, 2001\. CAS pioneered a customer\-focused security model built on a highly trained, professional workforce supported by competitive wages, benefits, and ongoing development.
  
Today, CAS is the largest private contractor providing Screening Partnership Program (SPP) services to the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) and an industry leader in aviation security solutions. Through its commitment to safety, compliance, operational excellence, and customer service, CAS provides comprehensive security and screening services for airports, airlines, and government agencies across the United States.
  
Employment Compensation \& Benefits
  
Covenant Aviation Security offers a competitive compensation package, with a targeted compensation range of $60,000 \- $75,000 annually depending on qualifications, experience, and contract requirements.

jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Why this role is on the menu

Instacart is building a best-in-class Internal Audit function from the ground up, and this role is central to it. This leader would add the structure, rigor, and technical depth required to deliver risk-based IT audit engagements at executive-quality standards.

Reporting directly to the Head of Internal Audit, this Director will own end-to-end IT audit delivery while building the function's technology capability and strategic priorities.

This role is for a seasoned Internal Audit professional who combines deep technical judgment with strong business acumen, excellent communication skills, a collaborative approach, and the drive to build something meaningful.

What You'll Cook Up In Your First Year

Audit Delivery & Reporting

IT audit and advisory engagements are delivered end-to-end with executive-quality standards, clear ownership, and defensible scope.
Independent audit judgment is applied consistently across engagements. Scope is calibrated to actual risk exposure, root cause analysis is rigorous, and conclusions are well-evidenced — not driven by checkbox compliance.
Risk and control frameworks are applied with sound judgment, and findings are translated into clear, actionable narratives that resonate with both technical and non-technical audiences.
Hands-on expertise with cloud and data platforms — including AWS, GCP, Datadog, and Okta — is applied to assess controls and design practical, effective solutions across key environments.

Team Leadership & Development

A high-performing audit team is developed through structured coaching, clear expectations, and tailored development plans, with a culture of excellence, continuous learning, and proactive problem-solving taking hold.

AI, Technology & Innovation

AI risk and governance considerations — including GenAI and agentic AI model risk, bias, transparency, and data privacy — are integrated into the audit approach.
AI-enabled tools and data analytics are adopted to expand coverage, improve efficiency, and enhance audit impact.

Tools & Process Improvement

The Workiva platform is fully implemented and administered, anchoring the function's first-time build of a risk-based Internal Audit operating model aligned to IIA Standards.
Controls are streamlined, manual effort is reduced, and operational efficiency across the audit function improves.

Stakeholder Partnerships

Productive relationships are built and maintained with business leaders and cross-functional partners — including Finance, Legal, ERM, Compliance, IT, Engineering, and Security — to implement scalable controls.
This role serves as a trusted advisor across technology and data teams, shaping audit approaches for complex, AI-driven environments.

The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have Pantry Staples (Minimum Qualifications)

12-15 years of progressive professional experience, with at least 5 years in a leadership role overseeing IT risk-based audits at a high-growth, global company.
Demonstrated experience building a risk-based Internal Audit function from the ground up, with working knowledge of IIA Standards and the ability to apply them in practice.
Track record of delivering risk-based audits in a fast-paced, agile technology environment with competing priorities and evolving risk landscapes.
Exceptional written communication skills. Able to produce executive-quality audit reports with minimal revision and translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable narratives.
Collaborative, relationship-oriented approach with the ability to influence and partner effectively across all levels of the organization.
Translate deep technical expertise into impactful, actionable insights that resonate with both technical and non-technical audiences.

Optional Garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

CISA, CRISC, or CIA certification. One or more of these designations is strongly preferred for this role.

jobs.description:
For over 70 years, Delrin® has been the trusted choice for engineers who demand high-performance materials. Our acetal homopolymer empowers innovative product design with superior mechanical properties, unmatched machinability, and design flexibility. We provide materials, knowledge, and collaboration to achieve breakthroughs that build a better future.

Delrin® is an engineering plastic/polymer used by our customers for many crucial components in highly engineered and technical applications, largely replacing metal with more efficient and cost-effective solutions that last as long. We have a strong focus on sustainability and produce a portion of our products from 100% bio feedstocks.

Delrin® Job Description

Chief Information Security Officer

Job Description

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) is responsible for overseeing the information security needs of the company. You will develop and oversee a comprehensive information security strategy that protects the company from all internal and external threats, while ensuring that the company adheres to all applicable cyber security regulatory, contractual, customer, and audit requirements. You will be required to stay up-to-date on emerging threats and security technologies and partner with the IT, OT, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, and business organizations to implement modern cyber security solutions.

In addition, the CISO will own the company’s cyber security incident response program and prepares the company for potential cyber-attacks through documented response plans, testing, training, and executive tabletop exercises. The CISO is accountable for cyber security strategy, governance, risk management, policies, standards, and oversight. IT (Information Technology), OT (Operational Technology), application, data, and business teams remain responsible for operating their respective systems and implementing security controls in accordance with the company’s cyber security requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and implement a comprehensive information security strategy aligned with the company’s business objectives, risk tolerance, and IT and OT priorities.
Establish and maintain a global cyber security governance framework covering IT, OT, cloud, network, application, identity, endpoint, and data security.
Ensure that IT and OT security controls adhere to applicable regulatory, contractual, customer, audit, and company requirements.
Own the company’s cyber security risk management program and risk register, including risk identification, treatment, acceptance, remediation, and regular executive reporting.
Own and maintain the company’s cyber security incident response program, including preparation, escalation, communication, investigation, containment, recovery, corrective action, tabletop exercises, and periodic testing.
Oversee continuous security monitoring, threat detection, vulnerability management, incident triage, and remediation through internal teams, IT and OT organizations, and managed security service providers.
Develop security architecture requirements, policies, standards, and control objectives for IT and OT systems in partnership with IT Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications, Data and Analytics, site OT leadership, and other technology stakeholders.
Provide cyber security governance and guidance for network segmentation, remote access, identity and access management, cloud services, endpoints, applications, data protection, backup protection, and industrial control environments.
Partner with IT Operations, application teams, and site OT teams to ensure security controls are implemented, maintained, monitored, and continuously improved within the systems and networks they operate.
Create, implement, maintain, and enforce IT and OT security policies, protocols, standards, procedures, responsibilities, decision rights, and escalation paths.
Manage IT security personnel and oversee managed security service providers, Security Operations Center services, security vendors, and other external providers, including performance, escalation, control effectiveness, and continuous improvement.
Lead cyber security audit, assessment, and evidence coordination activities, including regulatory audits, IT general controls audits, customer security assessments, internal assessments, external inquiries, and remediation tracking.
Establish and oversee third-party cyber security risk management, including due diligence, risk assessments, contractual requirements, ongoing monitoring, vendor negotiations, and remediation.
Develop and oversee the company’s cyber security awareness and training program, including phishing awareness, employee and contractor training, completion metrics, and education for higher-risk roles.
Develop and manage the cyber security budget, resource plans, investment priorities, metrics, and key risk indicators, and communicate security posture, emerging threats, costs, business value, and risk reduction to executive leadership and appropriate governance bodies.

Ideal Profile

A bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, cyber security, risk management, or a related field. An MBA or relevant advanced degree is preferable.
A minimum of nine years' experience in risk management, information security, cyber security, IT, OT security, or a related field, including leadership experience.
Knowledge of information security management frameworks, such as ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST.
Experience developing enterprise cyber security strategies, governance frameworks, policies, standards, risk registers, and incident response programs.
Experience working with IT and OT organizations in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
Experience overseeing Security Operations Center services, managed security service providers, incident response, vulnerability management, and security remediation.
Experience supporting regulatory, customer, internal, and external cyber security audits and assessments.
Experience with third-party cyber security risk management, customer security assurance, and cyber security contractual requirements.
Outstanding negotiation skills for negotiating contracts and security support services to be rendered.
Excellent understanding of current legislation, regulations, contractual obligations, and industry requirements relevant to our organization.
Excellent project management, risk management, and leadership skills.
Ability to communicate technical cyber security risks in business terms and clearly explain costs, value, risk reduction, and recommended actions to executive leadership.
First-rate written and verbal communication skills.
Based in Wilmington, DE or remote in other locations

We offer: 

An exciting opportunity to make an impact in a dynamic and growth-oriented company.
A competitive remuneration package, including generous benefits.

Our culture is grounded on the foundations of Stewardship, People, Growth, and Excellence, guiding us as we engineer a better future, together.

Stewardship - We embrace stewardship, upholding the safety and wellbeing of our people, our customers and our communities.
People - We empower our people, fostering a culture of respect, empowerment and continuous development.
Growth - We focus on growth, embracing innovation and adaptability to expand possibilities for our customers and our business.
Excellence - We drive excellence, achieving superior results through agile execution and advanced solutions.

Delrin is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage qualified candidates of all backgrounds to apply for this exciting opportunity to join our team and contribute to our continued success.

jobs.title: Head of IT Strategy and Transformation
jobs.description:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.

Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

Head of the IT Strategy and Transformation Office (STO) leads an integrated enterprise capability that connects strategy, architecture, investment planning, delivery excellence, organizational change, and executive governance. The role brings Enterprise Architecture, Lean Portfolio Management, Agile Delivery (LACE), Organizational Change Management, and Executive Governance together into one accountable operating model. Through this leadership, the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation ensures technology investments are strategically aligned, architecturally sound, appropriately prioritized, delivery-ready, and supported through adoption. The role connects enterprise strategy to execution by enabling informed decisions, focusing resources on the highest-value work, and improving transparency, consistency, and accountability for transformation outcomes.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Leads the Integrated IT Strategy & Transformation Office

Sets the strategic agenda and annual operating plan for the STO, unifying architecture, portfolio, delivery, and governance activity behind one coherent enterprise strategy.
Owns the end-to-end operating model connecting strategy formulation, investment funding, architectural standards, delivery execution, and governance decision rights.
Serves as the single executive point of accountability for whether the organization's technology investments collectively advance its strategic priorities — through the quality of the recommendations, architecture, and delivery readiness the STO brings forward, not through unilateral funding authority.
Represents the STO to the executive team, the Investment Council, and Board-level committees, translating strategic intent into well-formed, architected, and delivery-ready investment recommendations for those bodies to decide.

Enterprise Architecture

Directs the definition of enterprise architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and reference architectures that ensure every investment advances one coherent strategy.
Establishes the architecture governance model — including an Architecture Review Board that evaluates major initiatives for strategic fit, technical risk, and reuse before funding is committed — and delegates day-to-day chairmanship of the Board to the Principal Architect.
Owns the technology rationalization and modernization roadmap, reducing redundant platforms and technical debt over time.

Lean Portfolio Management

Directs enterprise investment planning, aligning funding, capacity, and prioritization with strategic themes and value streams.
Facilitates the Investment Council — a standing committee of executive leaders who hold formal decision-making authority over funding, sequencing, and re-prioritization of major initiatives — by preparing prioritized investment recommendations, portfolio trade-off analysis, and capacity/value data for the committee's decisions. The Head of IT Strategy & Transformation does not hold personal or unilateral funding decision rights.
Owns portfolio-level value realization: tracking benefits, cost, and capacity against plan, and reallocating investment as strategic priorities shift.

Agile Delivery (LACE)

Builds and matures enterprise delivery capability through the Lean-Agile Center of Excellence — coaching, engineering practices, and operating model maturity across delivery teams.
Scope note: LACE owns the ways of working and delivery-team practices used to build initiatives; it does not own business-side adoption of the resulting process or operational changes — that responsibility sits with Organizational Change Management, below.
Sets delivery standards and operating cadences (e.g., Program Increment planning, Scrum of Scrums) that give the portfolio a predictable, transparent delivery rhythm.
Establishes delivery KPIs (predictability, flow, quality, cycle time) and drives continuous improvement across delivery teams.

Executive Governance

Personally designs, chairs, and runs the decision forums and escalation paths that connect strategy, investment, architecture, and execution — including cadence, membership, and decision rights for each forum. This is not delegated to a direct-report manager; the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation is the accountable owner of governance.
Ensures every major decision (funding, architecture exception, delivery risk) is made in the right forum, by the right owner, with the right information, and personally facilitates the highest-stakes / executive-level sessions.
Publishes and maintains a governance operating calendar and RACI so accountability is explicit at every level of the model; may be supported by governance/PMO analysts for administration and reporting, but retains direct ownership of the function.
Serves as the escalation point of last resort within the STO for unresolved cross-discipline conflicts (e.g., architecture vs. delivery timeline, portfolio priority disputes).

Organizational Change Management

Owns enterprise-level change leadership for the operational and process-related impacts of major initiatives on the business — how work gets done, roles change, and processes are re-designed — as distinct from LACE's focus on delivery-team ways of working.

Directs the Manager, Organizational Change Management to build and run a repeatable OCM methodology (stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment, communication planning, training, and adoption measurement) applied consistently across major initiatives.

Ensures every initiative entering the portfolio carries a change-readiness assessment and a named change plan before it is funded, closing a common gap where technical delivery outpaces organizational readiness.

Personally sponsors change management for the STO's own operating model — leading the organization through the shift to a unified strategy, architecture, portfolio, and governance function, including communication, training, and adoption of new decision rights and cadences.

Partners with HR, Communications, and business-unit leaders to align change plans with broader organizational initiatives and to manage change fatigue across concurrent transformations.

Establishes adoption and sentiment metrics (e.g., stakeholder readiness scores, training completion, adoption rates) and reviews them alongside delivery and portfolio KPIs so change outcomes are tracked with the same rigor as cost and schedule.

Team Leadership and Development

Provides strategic, tactical, and day-to-day direction to the architecture, portfolio, delivery, and change management leads who report into the STO.

Builds a cohesive leadership team across historically separate disciplines, establishing shared metrics, cadence, and a common operating language — while personally modeling the governance standard the team is held to, since the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation owns that discipline directly.

Owns hiring, performance management, coaching, and development planning for direct reports; holds them accountable for the same standard across their functions.

Manages the STO's budget, staffing, and vendor/consulting resources, and ensures adherence to company policy and compliance requirements.

Acts as an escalation point and thought partner for the organization on complex, cross-functional strategy, architecture, portfolio, or delivery problems.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Directly supervises the leaders of Enterprise Architecture, Lean Portfolio Management, Agile Delivery (LACE), and Organizational Change Management, and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. Executive Governance is run by the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation directly and has no dedicated manager. Supervisory responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training team members; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining staff; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing direct reports and their teams; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations and goals; forecasting staffing needs across the STO; and enforcing department policies and procedures.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university required, in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field; Master's degree (MBA or equivalent) preferred.
Minimum 12 years of progressive experience across enterprise architecture, portfolio management, agile delivery, or IT/business strategy.
Minimum 7 years in a leadership role managing multidisciplinary teams and/or a Strategy, Transformation, PMO, or Enterprise Architecture function.
Demonstrated track record building or leading a Lean Portfolio Management model, Agile Center of Excellence, or comparable transformation function.

CERTIFICATES AND LICENSES

SAFe Program Consultant (SPC) or SAFe Agilist required; SAFe Lean Portfolio Management (LPM) certification preferred. TOGAF or equivalent enterprise architecture certification preferred. Prosci Change Management Certification or equivalent OCM credential preferred. PMP, PgMP, or ITIL certification a plus.

Knowledge And Skills

Deep working knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks, Lean Portfolio Management, SAFe or comparable scaled-agile operating models, and executive governance design.
Proven ability to translate enterprise strategy into a funded, architected, and delivery-ready portfolio of initiatives.
Skilled at designing governance forums, decision rights, and operating cadences that hold a large organization accountable without adding bureaucracy.
Strong financial acumen — able to build, defend, and manage a multidisciplinary budget and demonstrate portfolio-level value realization.
Exceptional executive communication and influence skills; able to synthesize complex, cross-functional trade-offs into clear recommendations for senior leadership and the Board.
Experience leading organizational change across historically siloed functions, building one shared operating culture out of separate disciplines.
Hands-on knowledge of organizational change management methodology (e.g., Prosci ADKAR or equivalent) and demonstrated ability to personally sponsor change on high-visibility, enterprise-wide initiatives.

Physical Requirements

This job operates in a professional office environment. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently will sit, stand, walk, and bend during working hours. Requires manual and finger dexterity and eye-hand coordination. May be required to lift light objects. Requires normal or corrected vision and hearing corrected to a normal range.

Overview

The Director, IT is responsible for leading the organization’s IT operations, technology services, and overall IT strategy. This role provides leadership and direction across IT support, infrastructure, systems administration, cybersecurity, identity and access management, and technology operations to ensure reliable, secure, and effective technology services across the organization.

Operating with a high degree of autonomy, the Director, IT establishes priorities, develops and maintains IT standards and processes, manages technology risks, and ensures IT services align with business needs and organizational objectives. This position serves as a senior technology leader and trusted partner to stakeholders across the organization.

This role requires a strong balance of strategic leadership, operational oversight, technical knowledge, and people leadership. The Director, IT is responsible for building a responsive and accountable IT function, driving continuous improvement, and ensuring a consistently positive experience for employees and business partners.

Responsibilities

IT Leadership & Strategy

Develop and execute the IT strategy and roadmap in alignment with organizational priorities and business objectives.
Lead day-to-day IT operations and ensure the effective delivery of reliable, secure, and scalable technology services.

Support compliance initiatives and ensure IT practices align with applicable security and compliance requirements, including PCI and SOC controls.

Develop and manage technology lifecycle and replacement strategies.
Manage relationships with IT vendors, service providers, and technology partners.
Evaluate vendor performance, contracts, licensing, and service agreements.
Support budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning for IT resources and initiatives.

Build a culture of accountability, responsiveness, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Establish appropriate roles, responsibilities, and operating practices within the IT function.
Support professional development, training, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
Recruit and retain IT talent with the skills required to support the organization’s evolving technology needs.
Foster effective collaboration between IT and other departments across the organization.

Translate business requirements into practical technology solutions.
Provide guidance and recommendations to leadership on technology opportunities, risks, and investments.

jobs.title: Director, TA Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the Team

Talent Acquisition & Management at ServiceNow is building the systems and strategy behind AI-native hiring at scale. As we bring our new Avature platform online this December, we need someone to own what happens next: the day-to-day design, operations, and TA Tech vendor relationships that keep our foundational TA systems running well and running smart.

About The Role

We're looking for a true subject-matter expert who can bridge deep TA process knowledge with strong systems and vendor management skills, someone who makes sure the technology recruiters rely on every day just works and keeps getting better. You'll work in constant partnership with Product and DT, and be the voice of TA in those rooms: someone who understands how recruiters actually source, screen, and move candidates, and who can translate a system change into what it means for hiring velocity and candidate experience. You'll own the future strategy design and day-to-day operations of Avature and our other foundational TA&M systems and program partnerships as we bring them online, acting as the translator between our business strategy and the systems that power it.

What You'll Own

Avature Post-Implementation: full ownership of platform optimization, adoption, and operational excellence following our December go-live, including vendor relationship management and quarterly business reviews.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: serving as the primary liaison between TA, the Project Madagascar program team, and People Product & DT, translating technical requirements into what they mean for the TA practitioner.
TA Technology Stack Optimization: governance and design for our foundational TA systems (Avature, LinkedIn, HackerRank, Findem and more as we bring new tools online), ensuring interoperability and long-term reliability, with Customer Zero and Now on Now top of mind, always looking for where we can lean further into our own ServiceNow platform as part of our broader strategy heading into next year.
Pre-Go-Live Implementation Readiness: partnering with the Project Madagascar change team on training, documentation, cutover planning, and day-one support.
Vendor Relationship Management: receiving vendor handoffs from our Innovation team and owning ongoing partnership, SLA accountability, contract renewals, and optimization conversations.
Operational Metrics & Governance: establishing and tracking system health, adoption, and performance KPIs that feed directly into our roadmap decisions.

Qualifications

What You'll Bring

Background in TA technology, operations, and strategy; Avature experience is strongly preferred.
Prior experience as a recruiter or sourcing practitioner is a big plus; it's what lets you speak the language of the team you're serving.
A track record of owning vendor relationships and driving system adoption at scale.
Expert-level collaboration skills and cross-functional experience; there are strong relationships between our TA CoE, Product and DT teams and connectedness while working as a team is a critical piece of this role.
The judgment to operate independently while staying tightly aligned with TA strategy.

Additional Information

Work Personas

We approach our distributed world of work with flexibility and trust. Work personas (flexible, remote, or required in office) are categories that are assigned to ServiceNow employees depending on the nature of their work and their assigned work location. Learn more here. To determine eligibility for a work persona, ServiceNow may confirm the distance between your primary residence and the closest ServiceNow office using a third-party service.

Equal Opportunity Employer

ServiceNow is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, gender identity, veteran status, or any other category protected by law. In addition, all qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with legal requirements.

Accommodations

We strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application process, or are unable to use this online application and need an alternative method to apply, please contact globaltalentss@servicenow.com for assistance.

Export Control Regulations

For positions requiring access to controlled technology subject to export control regulations, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), ServiceNow may be required to obtain export control approval from government authorities for certain individuals. All employment is contingent upon ServiceNow obtaining any export license or other approval that may be required by relevant export control authorities.

jobs.title: Director, IT
jobs.description:
DNSFilter's mission is to protect our customers and partners with products they love to use! We are revolutionizing network security by providing fast, accurate, and reliable threat protection and content filtering. We're a rapidly growing company dedicated to creating a safer internet for businesses and organizations worldwide. Leveraging AI\-driven threat intelligence, DNSFilter empowers our customers to proactively block threats before they impact their networks. We foster a collaborative, innovative, and results\-oriented culture where every team member contributes to our mission of making the internet safer.



We are a security company, and how we run our own systems should reflect that. Our internal IT function has kept pace with a growing company through automation rather than headcount, and it is ready for someone to own it end to end. That's where you come in!


**We are looking for a Director of IT, based in our Tampa office, to own internal identity, endpoints, and employee technology at DNSFilter. This is a hands\-on leadership role, not an oversight role. You will run Okta, Google Workspace, and our MDM platforms yourself while leading one Senior IT Support Analyst, and you will be accountable for whether our controls actually work, not just whether they are configured. The ideal candidate has built an IT function at this stage before, is comfortable in the consoles, and would rather automate a recurring problem than staff it.**


**This role reports to the SVP of Operations and partners closely with Security, People, Finance, and every department that depends on getting access to their tools on day one.**  

  

**This is a full\-time hybrid\-office role for our Tampa (Westchase), Florida office.**

  

**Eligible candidates have worked successfully in a small\- to mid\-sized, fast\-paced, hyper\-growth SaaS start\-up or scale\-up.**



We recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If you feel like this job is for you, please apply. We believe diversity of experience and skills, including transferable skills, combined with passion, is a key to innovation and excellence; therefore, we encourage people from all backgrounds to apply to our positions!


**In this role, you will:**


**Identity and Access**


* Own Okta day to day: user administration, SSO configuration, app assignments, MFA policy implementation, lifecycle rules, and Okta Desktop MFA across the fleet
* Own Google Workspace administration, including groups, distribution lists, delegated access, and directory hygiene
* Own the onboarding, offboarding, and change management lifecycle end to end, and be accountable for the number that says access was actually revoked on time
* Partner with Security to define, and own the operation of, the access model for contractors and BYOD users, including what they can reach, how it is isolated from personal use, and how access and company data end when an engagement does
* Reduce the volume of manual access requests through automation, group\-based entitlements, and self\-service, rather than by working the queue faster


**Endpoint and Fleet**


* Own Mosyle for Apple and JumpCloud for everything else: enrollment, configuration profiles, app deployment, patch posture, and device inventory
* Ensure every company device is enrolled through a supervised path, and close the gaps where it is not
* Maintain accurate fleet coverage reporting, including whether our own machines run DNSFilter's Roaming Client under an enforcing policy
* Support the Security team's rollout of endpoint security tooling on the devices you manage


**Asset Lifecycle**


* Own hardware end to end: procurement through Insight and CDW, zero\-touch enrollment and provisioning, asset tagging, drop\-ship to employees, and return logistics
* Redeploy returned devices under three years old before ordering new, and route anything three years or older to certified recycling
* Maintain an accurate record of every deployed device that reconciles to headcount, MDM, and Finance's asset register
* Manage warranty, repair, and replacement, and own the refresh cycle and the budget behind it
* Own retirement: secure wipe, certified disposal, and the documentation that proves a device was sanitized before it left our hands
* Own device recovery from departing employees and contractors, including the follow\-up on equipment that has not been returned


**Application Portfolio and Spend**


* Own the full inventory of business applications, including what sits outside SSO and how it got there
* Manage licenses against actual usage, reclaim what is unused, and bring renewals forward with a recommendation rather than an invoice
* Own the IT budget: build it, forecast it, and be able to explain why spend moved
* Own IT vendor relationships and contracts, and make the call when a tool is no longer earning its cost


**Workplace Technology**


* Own the technology in our Tampa office: the Ubiquiti stack end to end, including UniFi network and wifi, Access with facial recognition entry, and Protect cameras
* Own physical access and surveillance systems in partnership with People Ops and Security, including who has access to what, retention of footage, and handling of biometric data
* Own conference room AV, printers, and shared office equipment
* Make in\-office and hybrid meetings work reliably, because the ones that do not are the ones everyone remembers


**Service Delivery**


* Own the Zendesk helpdesk: intake, taxonomy, priority definitions, SLAs, and customer satisfaction measurement
* Report a small set of IT metrics monthly, and be the person who explains the number when it moves the wrong way
* Publish a service catalog so the company knows what IT does, how to ask for it, and what to expect


**Availability and Continuity**


* Define and run the escalation path for IT incidents, including lockouts, outages, and issues that hit people while travelin

jobs.description:
**Summary**
-----------


This position is in the U.S. Department of Education (ED), Federal Student Aid (FSA), Technology Operations Division (TOD). The Technology Operations Division provides information technology operations services for all FSA systems, promoting the effective and secure use of technology to achieve FSA's strategic objectives through sound planning, investments, integrated technology architectures and standards, effective systems development, production support, and cybersecurity services.


Learn more about this agency


  
**This job is open to**
-----------------------


### **The public**


U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.
### **Clarification from the agency**


This announcement is open to all U.S. Citizens. This is an excepted service position. All applicants who meet the qualification requirements will be forwarded to the selecting official for further consideration. Category Rating, Schedule A and traditional rating and ranking of applicants does not apply to this vacancy.


  
**Duties**
----------


**APPLICATION LIMIT:** This vacancy announcement is limited to the first 200 applications received and will close at 11:59PM Eastern Time on the day that we receive the 200 application, or at 11:59PM Eastern Time on the listed closing date, whichever occurs first.  

  

This position is eligible for Remote/Virtual work. However, this position may fall under the Presidential Memorandum titled "Return to In\-Person Work" which will require you to go into the office if you are located within 50 miles of a Department of Education facility in these locations: Washington, DC, Dallas, TX, San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, Kansas City, MO, Chicago, Il, Atlanta, GA, Philadelphia, PA, New York City, NY, and location is negotiable. Actual salary will be based on location of selectee. Locality pay tables available at www.opm.gov .  

  

We encourage you to read this entire vacancy announcement prior to submitting your application.  

  

**As a Chief Information Security Officer AD\-2210\-00 (Senior Manager), you will be responsible for:**


* Serving as the principal advisor to leadership and acts as an Authorizing Official (AO) / Designated Representative under FISMA, establishing agency\-wide IT security policies, managing enterprise cyber risk, and aligning security strategies with Department and OMB mandates.
* Directing Security Operations Center (SOC) capabilities\-including SIEM, network forensics, automated surveillance, and threat intelligence\-to detect, analyze, and mitigate cyber threats, expedite incident response, and protect high\-value assets and sensitive PII.
* Overseeing vulnerability management, Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation (CDM), and Authority to Operate (ATO) processes across cloud/data center hosting environments and enterprise applications, while enforcing strict cybersecurity contract standards across thousands of external partners and contractors.
* Leading cybersecurity audit response and remediation across OIG, DHS, and federal oversight bodies; manages security budgets and contractor performance; and provides comprehensive executive supervision, mentorship, and workforce planning for assigned cybersecurity personnel.
* Serving as the liaison and overseer of all FISMA, Financial, Office of the Inspector General, Department of Homeland Security, and other security audits.

----------------

In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider: \- your performance and conduct; \- the needs and interests of the agency; \- whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and \- whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service. Upon completion of your probationary period OR trial period your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

  

***Remove the Key Requirements that are not applicable:***  

  

**Key Requirements:**
* Must be a US Citizen.


* Males 18 and over must be registered with the Selective Service.


* Must complete a Background Investigation and Fingerprint check.


* May be required to successfully complete a two\-year trial period.


* Must be determined suitable for federal employment.


* Relocation expenses will not be paid.


* You may be subject to serve a one\-year supervisory probationary period.


* This position is subject to drug testing.


**You must meet all qualification requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this vacancy announcement.**

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
**Position Overview:** The Director of IT provides leadership and strategic direction for Circle of Life's technology operations and services. This position leads the organization's IT team, establishes priorities, manages resources, and ensures technology effectively supports the needs and goals of the organization. The Director partners with leadership across Circle of Life to evaluate opportunities, improve processes, manage technology initiatives, and ensure reliable, secure, and effective IT services. This role is responsible for building a strong IT function that supports organizational growth, innovation, and the delivery of quality services.

**Required Education and Experience:** A Bachelor's degree in a computer\-related field (with a major in Computer Sciences, information systems, or computer information systems) is required. Master's degree is preferred. Minimum 3 years of progressive leadership experience preferably in healthcare. Demonstrated ability to successfully lead teams through change. Knowledge of local, state and federal regulations related to information storage and cyber security; specialized computer skills, including experience with operating systems, computer hardware, networking, AI applications. Excellent communication skills, with ability to assign work and monitor employee performance. Ability to process information and analyze data, abilities in deductive reasoning and oral and written expression; Ability to explain technical subjects to staff without technical expertise. Ability to direct the work of other IT professionals and contractors. Ability to plan and coordinate activities such as installing and upgrading hardware and software, programming and systems design, the implementation of computer networks, and the development of internet and intranet websites. Ability to analyze the computer and information needs of the organization from an operational and strategic perspective and determine immediate and long\-range personnel and equipment requirements. Ability to assign and review the work of subordinates and stay abreast of the latest technology to ensure the organization's IT and IS needs are met. Excellent communicationpresentation skills and the ability to provide technical training to end\-users in the agency. 2\+ year's prior experience in healthcare IT preferred.


**SPECIFIC DUTIES AND POSITION REQUIREMENTS**

* Develops IS and IT infrastructure design and a strategic plan that accounts for future growth and technology evolution.
* Provide leadership and oversight to IT Manager and Software Specialist and ultimately all department personnel.
* Provide network design, installation, monitoring, management, and troubleshooting for WAN and LANs including main locations and remote sites.
* Ensure organization wide competency and knowledge related to the operation and maintenance of IT hardware and software systems, phone systems, building security systems, connectivity, and cellular phone operations.
* Implement and maintain a testing and education program to ensure network users are aware of network threats and how to avoid them.
* Develops and regularly reviews department budget and adjusts as needed.
* Regularly reviews and evaluates whether current infrastructure and applications are meeting the needs of the organization.
* Manages training and orientation content to ensure all network users are proficient with usage and security measures.
* Schedules upgrades and security backups of hardware and software systems.
* Maintain current and accurate inventory of technology hardware, software and resources.
* Collaborate with Executive Team and other Managers to gain input on improving IS solutions and end\-user equipment.
* Research and implement new systems and/or programs as needed.
* Identify and prepare hardware for disposal when appropriate, and ensure hardware is stripped and secured before disposal.
* Work with multiple vendors to obtain competitive pricing for goods and services.
* Regularly provides troubleshooting support to network users.
* Demonstrates compassion, empathy, and patience when interacting with patients, families, co\-workers, and members of the public.
* Represents Circle of Life to the community in a positive manner.
* Demonstrates flexibility, versatility and a positive attitude in integrating additional duties.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**About Us**

The North Carolina Community College System (System Office) is a statewide network of 58 public community colleges. The system enrolls over 500,000 students annually. It is the 3rd largest in the nation based on the number of colleges. It also provides data to the North Carolina Learning Object Repository by collecting, contributing, and sharing digital learning resources for use in traditional or distance learning environments. The mission of the North Carolina Community College System is to open the door to high\-quality, accessible educational opportunities that minimize barriers to post\-secondary education, maximize student success, develop a global, multicultural, and competent workforce, and improve the lives and wellbeing of N.C. citizens.
