Overview

As the Global Operational Technology (OT) Domain Architect, you will define and govern the architecture strategy, standards, reference architectures, and technology roadmaps for PepsiCo's Operational Technology landscape. You will provide architecture leadership across IT/OT convergence, OT architecture governance, OT data & information architecture, OT systems management (OTSM), Industry 4.0 architecture enablement, and OT modernization strategy initiatives supporting PepsiCo's operational environments across Manufacturing, Warehousing, and other operational technology-enabled environments.

You will partner with Engineering, Controls Engineering, Infrastructure, Network Engineering, Compute & Hosting, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, Product, Transformation, and Domain Architecture teams to define integrated architecture strategies, standards, and roadmaps supporting secure, resilient, scalable, and future-ready operational technology ecosystems.

You will serve as the primary architecture leader for the OT domain, ensuring alignment across operational technology, enterprise technology, automation, and emerging Industry 4.0 capabilities through architecture standards, governance frameworks, reference architectures, and technology roadmaps.

Responsibilities

OT Domain Strategy & Architecture:

Define and maintain the Operational Technology domain strategy, standards, reference architectures, principles, and multi-year technology roadmaps.
Establish architecture direction supporting IT/OT convergence, OT modernization, operational resiliency, and future operational technology capabilities.
Evaluate emerging operational technologies in partnership with Technology Strategy, Innovation, and Engineering teams, and define scalable adoption approaches aligned to enterprise standards, business priorities, and long-term technology strategy.
Define architecture enablement strategies supporting Industry 4.0 initiatives including industrial AI, robotics, autonomous operations, advanced sensing, industrial automation, and future operational technologies.

Define architecture frameworks supporting convergence of IT and OT capabilities while maintaining operational safety, reliability, availability, and security requirements.

Facilitate cross-functional architecture alignment across Engineering, Operations, Infrastructure, Security, Data & AI, and Enterprise Architecture teams.

Establish architecture principles that balance enterprise consistency with OT requirements for operational continuity and low-latency environments.
Define reference architectures supporting integrated IT/OT operating models and governance frameworks.
Promote architectural consistency and standardization across operational environments globally.

OT Data Strategy & Information Architecture:

Define OT data architecture principles, information models, classification standards, interoperability requirements, and architecture governance frameworks.
Partner with Data & AI teams to align OT information architecture and data integration requirements with enterprise data standards and platforms.
Define architecture patterns supporting OT data acquisition, integration, visibility, observability, and interoperability across operational technology and enterprise technology environments.

Establish reference architectures supporting asset discovery, observability, monitoring, operational support, and OT lifecycle capabilities.
Define architecture patterns supporting industrial connectivity, operational intelligence, and future Industry 4.0 initiatives.
Guide technology modernization and rationalization efforts across operational technology environments while maintaining operational continuity.

Establish architecture standards, reference patterns, and integration approaches supporting interoperability across operational technology platforms and environments.
Support evaluation of technology options, modernization pathways, and platform strategies in collaboration with Engineering, Infrastructure, Security, Procurement, and Technology Strategy teams.

Act as the primary architecture integration point across operational technology and enterprise technology domains.
Lead OT architecture reviews and governance activities to ensure alignment with enterprise standards and strategic objectives.
Provide architecture leadership and consultation supporting operational technology initiatives globally.

jobs.title: Vice President, Product & Technology PMO
jobs.description:
About Powerfleet

Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. With more than 30 years of experience, Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonization, and integration of data—regardless of source—and delivers actionable insights to help companies meet their strategic objectives around Safety, Compliance, Efficiency and Sustainability. Our people-first culture and relentless innovation empower customers to achieve measurable, sustainable business improvements. Powerfleet serves over 2.6 million subscribers across more than 48,000 customers in 120 countries, with commercial operations across every major continent.

Position Summary

Powerfleet is seeking a Vice President, Product & Technology PMO to lead strategic portfolio management and execution across Product, Engineering, Technology, and enterprise transformation initiatives. This role will establish and drive the operating model, governance, and execution discipline needed to translate Powerfleet’s strategic priorities into measurable business and customer outcomes.

The Vice President, Product & Technology PMO will provide a single, integrated view of major initiatives across the organization, ensuring alignment around priorities, capacity, dependencies, investments, risks, and delivery. Partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and executive leadership, this role will strengthen portfolio decision-making, improve delivery predictability, and create clear accountability for outcomes.

The ideal candidate is a highly experienced technology and transformation leader who combines strong portfolio management expertise with business and financial acumen and thrives in a fast-paced, global environment.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Strategy & Governance

Lead the Product & Technology PMO, including program management, project management, scrum, and delivery resources.
Establish and maintain portfolio governance across Product, Engineering, Technology, and enterprise transformation initiatives.
Develop and manage annual and quarterly planning, prioritization, capacity, and investment processes.
Create a single executive view of strategic initiatives, including milestones, dependencies, risks, investments, resource requirements, and expected outcomes.
Establish clear governance, decision-making, and accountability frameworks to support effective portfolio execution.
Ensure strategic investments remain aligned with organizational priorities and measurable business and customer outcomes.

Program & Delivery Excellence

Partner closely with Product and Engineering leaders to improve roadmap execution, delivery predictability, and time-to-market.
Oversee major technology and enterprise transformation initiatives, ensuring effective planning, execution, and risk management.
Drive cross-functional execution across complex programs involving multiple business functions, technologies, geographies, and stakeholders.
Identify and proactively address organizational, resource, technology, and delivery dependencies that may impact strategic initiatives.
Establish consistent program and portfolio management practices while enabling teams to operate with appropriate flexibility and agility.
Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement across portfolio execution.

Executive Reporting & Performance Management

Develop executive dashboards and KPIs that provide clear visibility into portfolio health, delivery performance, investment, business value, and customer outcomes.
Provide executive leadership with timely, actionable insights into portfolio progress, risks, dependencies, and decisions required.
Establish mechanisms to measure value realization and business outcomes associated with strategic technology investments.
Improve transparency and consistency in how program performance and portfolio health are communicated across the organization.

Financial & Resource Management

Partner with Finance and executive leadership on portfolio investment decisions, resource allocation, capacity planning, and value realization.
Develop frameworks to evaluate and prioritize investments based on strategic alignment, expected value, resource requirements, and organizational capacity.
Monitor portfolio investments and resource utilization to support informed decision-making and effective allocation of resources.
Balance strategic priorities with available capacity to improve organizational focus and execution.

PMO Transformation & Innovation

Build and continuously evolve a modern, outcome-driven PMO focused on enabling execution rather than traditional project reporting.
Leverage automation, AI-enabled tools, and data-driven insights to improve planning, reporting, forecasting, risk management, and decision-making.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce administrative burden, and increase the speed and quality of portfolio decisions.
Establish scalable practices and tools that support Powerfleet’s continued growth and transformation.

Qualifications

15+ years of progressive experience across technology, product, program management, business transformation, and/or enterprise PMO leadership.
Significant experience leading global Product and Technology portfolios and complex, enterprise-wide transformation programs.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing program management, project management, scrum, and/or delivery teams.
Proven ability to partner effectively with C-suite executives and influence decisions across organizational and functional boundaries.
Strong understanding of software and product development, enterprise technology, and business transformation.
Experience supporting or leading major ERP, CRM, technology rationalization, SaaS, data, AI, and cloud initiatives.
Strong knowledge of portfolio management, strategic planning, capacity planning, resource allocation, and investment governance.
Demonstrated financial and business acumen, including experience evaluating investments and measuring value realization.
Strong executive communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex portfolio information into clear, actionable insights.
Experience implementing modern portfolio management practices, tools, automation, and data-driven reporting.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, global, highly cross-functional environment.
Builder mindset with demonstrated success establishing or transforming a PMO into a strategic, outcome-focused function.

Success in the Role

Success in this role will be demonstrated by establishing a transparent and integrated Product & Technology portfolio; improving delivery predictability, prioritization, and capacity management; strengthening visibility into investments, risks, and dependencies; and creating clear accountability for the outcomes of Powerfleet’s most important technology and business transformation initiatives. This leader will help make strategy executable, improve organizational focus, and create greater predictability across execution.

The annual salary range for this full-time position is $230,000- $250,000
USD. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on the candidate’s experience, skills, and location.

Powerfleet is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable law. We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation and success, and we’re proud to be a workplace that reflects the communities we serve.

Our end-to-end solutions help businesses monitor, manage, and optimize everything from warehouse assets to connected vehicles, driving safety, efficiency, and sustainability across the supply chain. Technical or data expertise is not required, but the position must be comfortable working with technical partners and managing data\-related initiatives. Supervision is provided by a Program Director, Programs Officer, or other designated MSPHI executive leader. Work is reviewed through meetings, reports, and evaluation of program outcomes.

Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey, is a leading national research university and the State of New Jersey’s preeminent, comprehensive public institution of higher education. Rutgers’ commitment to its employees includes maintaining and fostering a safe, diverse, and respectful workplace environment, creating employment opportunities for our nation’s military veterans, and ensuring accessibility and accommodation for individuals with disabilities.
  

**Posting Summary**
Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey is seeking a Director, Information Technology for the School of Environmental and Biological Sciences. Reporting to the Sr. Associate Dean for Finance and Administration, the IT Director provides strategic leadership and oversight of all information technology operations within the New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station (NJAES) and the School of Environmental and Biological Sciences (SEBS). This includes web development, IT research and innovation, information security, and advanced research computing. The position also has overall responsibility for the day\-to\-day management of the unit’s technological infrastructure, equipment, and associated staff and budgets.
  

  

The IT Director will ensure alignment between functional leads, departmental staff, and central university IT initiatives. This structure will foster improved communication, reduce redundancy, and enhance the efficiency and quality of IT services delivered to faculty, staff, and students. Ultimately, this approach balances the benefits of embedded departmental expertise with the advantages of coordinated, school\-wide IT governance. Working directly with the Office of the Chief Information Officer (CIO) and OIT leadership, the Director will receive institutional guidance and implement central IT policies and initiatives under the purview of the CIO’s office and will represent SEBS/NJAES in all OIT functional groups and committees as requested.
  

  

Working closely with the CIO’s office and university IT leadership, the Director provides timely, accurate, and strategic guidance to the administration, faculty, and staff of SEBS/NJAES with regard to technology needs, changes, and opportunities. Under the Director’s leadership, SEBS/NJAES researchers benefit from high\-performance computing resources, analytics, and custom software solutions that streamline data processing, web development, and laboratory management. The position also leads the Programming and Web Development Office, supporting faculty, staff, students, and research centers on campus and across the state. The Director ensures secure, scalable, and reliable systems; develops and enforces IT policies; and provides expert guidance on cybersecurity, infrastructure modernization, and emerging technologies. Representing SEBS/NJAES in university\-wide IT initiatives, the IT Director fosters innovation, efficiency, and data accessibility to advance the teaching, research, and outreach missions of the unit.

* Provides strategic direction and develops information technology policies, procedures and controls within the School and Station, ensuring compliance with university policies and standards.

* Serves as a liaison with local IT support units in departments that have decentralized control of IT.
* Serves as the chief liaison with the University Office of Information Technology and works collaboratively with university colleagues.

* Monitors and minimizes information security risks.
* Identifies specific needs of individual researchers, devises and revises technological solutions to meet ever changing needs and taking advantage of emerging technologies.
* Supervises the development of new technologies to enhance learning spaces for students and improve the capabilities available to instructors.
* Oversees project initiation, prioritization and resource allocation to ensure efficient workload distribution for web development projects.
* Provides oversight and serves as a liaison to executive management for large programming projects.
* Evaluates programming and web development techniques and provides final approval prior to deployment.
* Reviews all technical aspects of projects during the development phase to ensure compliance with coding, accessibility and documentation requirements.

We're hiring a Director of Information Security to lead our governance, data protection, privacy, and risk functions. This is a senior leadership role responsible for the programs that demonstrate we handle data responsibly — to customers, regulators, and the board. You'll own our compliance certifications, data security strategy, privacy program, and enterprise risk management, and you'll build and lead the team that runs them.


You'll operate as both a strategic leader and a program builder: setting direction, hiring and growing a team, and partnering across engineering, legal, product, and the executive team to make security and privacy a durable business advantage rather than a checkbox.


**What you'll do**
------------------


* Own and mature our compliance program end to end, including frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, and others relevant to our customers and markets, and lead audits to successful outcomes.
* Set data security strategy: data classification, access governance, encryption standards, DLP, and controls that protect sensitive and customer data across its lifecycle.
* Build and run the privacy program, ensuring compliance with regulations such as GDPR and CCPA/CPRA, and partner with legal on data processing, DPAs, and privacy\-by\-design.
* Establish and operate an enterprise risk management program: risk identification, assessment, treatment, and reporting to leadership and the board.
* Own the third\-party/vendor risk and customer trust functions, including security questionnaires, customer assurance, and the trust center.
* Develop, maintain, and enforce security policies, standards, and control frameworks, and drive continuous controls monitoring.
* Hire, lead, and grow a high\-performing team spanning GRC, privacy, and risk.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to executives and report regularly on security, privacy, and risk posture.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------


* Extensive experience in information security, GRC, privacy, or risk, including several years leading and building teams (typically 10\+ years total, with meaningful management experience).
* Proven track record owning compliance certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, or equivalent) and leading audits to completion.
* Deep knowledge of data protection and privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) and how to operationalize them.
* Strong grounding in risk management frameworks and enterprise risk programs.
* Excellent executive communication — able to translate risk into business terms for leadership and the board.
* Experience partnering across engineering, legal, product, and sales in a fast\-moving environment.

**Nice to have**

* Relevant certifications (CISSP, CIPP, CISM, CRISC, or similar).
* Experience scaling a compliance/privacy program through significant company growth.
* Familiarity with continuous compliance tooling and controls automation.
* Background supporting enterprise sales and customer security reviews.

**What success looks like**
---------------------------


Within your first year, you'll have a clear\-eyed view of our risk landscape, a maturing set of compliance and privacy programs, a team positioned to scale, and executive confidence in our security and privacy posture.


Salary: $240k

* **We are AI forward:** We help our clients build the future of Al and implement it in our own roles and workflow to amplify productivity.

Chief Technology Officer (CTO)

**AirParts Aero**  
**Northern Virginia / Washington, D.C. Area**  
**Executive Leadership \| Full\-Time**

Build the Technology Platform for the Future of Aviation Commerce

AirParts Aero is building the digital infrastructure for the global aerospace aftermarket.

We are creating a platform designed to connect aircraft operators, airlines, government customers, OEMs, distributors, MROs, repair stations, service providers, and aerospace suppliers through a unified commerce, data, and intelligence ecosystem.

We are looking for a **Chief Technology Officer** to help lead that transformation.

This is not a maintenance role.

We are looking for a deeply technical executive who can help define the architecture, engineering organization, development standards, and long\-term technology strategy behind a platform intended to operate at significant scale across the aerospace industry.

The right candidate will be both a **builder and a leader**—someone capable of setting long\-range technical direction while remaining close enough to the technology to challenge architecture, review critical decisions, and help solve difficult engineering problems alongside the team.

**What You Will Help Build**

AirParts is expanding beyond traditional ecommerce into a broader aerospace operating platform.

You will work directly with the CEO, Chief Strategy Officer, product leadership, operations, quality, and engineering teams to translate business requirements into durable technical systems.

The platform must bring together information from many different sources, including:

* OEM data
* Supplier feeds

* Government sources
* Historical transactions
* Seller\-provided product information

Experience with areas such as master data management, entity resolution, knowledge graphs, semantic search, or data provenance is highly valuable.

**AI**

Lead the technical strategy for AI across the AirParts platform.

Potential areas include:

* AI\-assisted search

* Document intelligence

* Classification and extraction
* Retrieval\-augmented generation

**Search \& Discovery**

Experience with enterprise search, semantic retrieval, search ranking, vector search, or graph\-based discovery is strongly desirable.

Build and lead a high\-performance engineering organization.

The CTO will establish and enforce strong development practices around:

The goal is to create an engineering organization capable of shipping quickly without sacrificing reliability or technical discipline.

**Infrastructure \& Scalability**

This position is located within the Office of Finance and Administration, leading the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO). The Chief Information Officer (CIO) serves as the highest\-ranking official in the agency for information technology/information management (IT/IM), strategic technological infrastructure, and artificial intelligence (AI) implementation. These agency\-wide initiatives are vital to EPA's ability to execute statutory responsibilities to protect public health and the environment.  

  

As the Chief Information Officer, the incumbent provides executive leadership to ensure a high level of organizational performance. The CIO will inspire a multidisciplinary team to move OCIO into the future by fostering innovation, sustaining a highly secure operating environment and pushing appropriate boundaries to help EPA meet its mission of protecting human health and the environment. The CIO is responsible for creating a unified IT/IM and AI vision and mission, and for leading OCIO strategic planning and performance accountability functions, including those associated with annual performance reports, strategic reviews, quarterly performance reports, organizational assessments, and continuous improvement work.  

  

Specific duties of the position include, but are not limited to:


* Serving as the EPA's Chief Information Officer, the incumbent will represent and advocate for the agency in high\-level Federal government\-wide forums, including White House functions. This includes providing guidance to senior leadership that fundamentally shapes agency\-wide policies and practices, and networking with key officials from Congress, other Federal agencies, state and local governments, and the private sector, along with preparing and delivering speeches to further stakeholder understanding of and support for EPA's information programs.
* Planning, developing, influencing, directing, and implementing major, agency\-wide programs. This includes evaluating the technical status of existing systems, analyzing trends in modern infrastructure, recommending efficiency initiatives based on long\-term organizational goals, and directing office actions on emerging challenges with national impact.
* Assessing technical needs, defining agency\-wide goals, developing program plans, establishing OCIO's organizational structure, and establishing overall IT/IM operating policies, priorities, and procedures. This includes designing long\- and short\-range projects, strategically allocating financial and human capital resources within budgetary limits, determining the optimum balance between intramural and extramural (contract and grant effort), and maintaining accountability for progress and performance of all IT/IM conducted or directed activities.
* Serving as EPA's Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer (CAIO), with executive responsibility over governance, risk management, and strategic deployment of artificial intelligence across all agency systems, software architecture, and IT initiatives so that they securely advance the agency's mission.
* Coordinating OCIO activities and data\-sharing with internal and external stakeholders, including representatives of foreign, State and municipal governments, other Federal agencies, industry, academia, and private organizations.
* Supervising a multidisciplinary team of about 300 federal employees and over 400 contractors. The incumbent will supervise career senior executives, managers, and supervisors in support of a geographically dispersed agency of more than 12,000 employees.

ElevationHR is supporting a leading Houston-based energy and utility organization seeking a Strategy Leader, Enterprise Technology
to help solve complex business and operational challenges and shape the technologies the enterprise will need over the next 1–5 years
.

This is not a traditional Project Manager, Program Manager, or IT operations role
.

We are looking for a technology strategist who can walk into an ambiguous business problem, understand how business and physical operation actually work, identify where technology can create meaningful value, establish the strategy, influence architecture and investment decisions, and help turn that strategy into programs that deliver measurable results.

The right person can move comfortably between an executive strategy discussion and a deep technical conversation spanning hardware, software, infrastructure, cloud, data, AI, cybersecurity, IoT/IIoT, edge, connected assets, and emerging technology
.

Partner with senior business and technology leaders to identify and solve complex enterprise and operational problems, including opportunities that have not yet become formal programs.
Develop 1–5 year technology strategies
connecting business priorities, enterprise architecture, emerging technology, investment decisions, and executable initiatives.
Analyze business and operational processes end to end to identify root causes, constraints, risks, and opportunities for technology-enabled improvement.
Evaluate the full technology ecosystem, from physical assets, sensors, edge and infrastructure to software, cloud, data, AI, cybersecurity, and digital platforms
.
Translate opportunities into business cases, architecture direction, investment priorities, technology roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.
Evaluate build, buy, integrate, partner, pilot, and scale
decisions based on business value rather than technology novelty.
Work across business, IT, engineering, architecture, data/AI, cybersecurity, vendors, and systems integrators to move strategy into execution.
Stay engaged through implementation and adoption to ensure technology produces measurable business and operational value.

What We're Looking For

Must Have

Significant experience developing enterprise technology strategy
and leading complex technology-enabled transformation.
Demonstrated breadth across both software/applications and hardware, infrastructure, IoT/IIoT, edge, connected assets, or physical technology
.
Experience taking initiatives from ambiguous business problem → strategy → architecture/investment decision → implementation → adoption → measurable value
.
Strong systems thinking across business processes, people, physical operations, data, software, infrastructure, and technology dependencies.
Experience personally advising CIOs, CTOs, VPs, Senior Directors, or comparable executives
on major technology, architecture, investment, or transformation decisions.
Technical depth across several areas such as enterprise architecture, cloud, infrastructure, software, data/AI, cybersecurity, IoT/IIoT, edge, or operational technology.
Ability to identify and shape opportunities where the problem, solution, or program has not already been defined
.
Strong executive communication with the ability to move naturally between business strategy, technical architecture, and measurable outcomes
.
Bachelor's degree in a relevant business, engineering, technology, or related discipline.

Preferred

Experience in utilities, energy, oil and gas, industrial, manufacturing, transportation, infrastructure, or another asset-intensive or mission-critical environment
.
Experience connecting digital technology to physical operations through IoT/IIoT, sensors, telemetry, edge, OT, automation, digital twins, computer vision, drones, GIS, or related technologies
.
Experience with operational resilience, high availability, emergency response, or other environments where technology directly affects physical operations or customers.
Experience taking emerging technologies or early-stage capabilities from concept or pilot into enterprise use.
Practical experience applying AI, machine learning, or intelligent automation
to real business problems.
Master's degree or MBA preferred.
Electric utility or transmission and distribution experience is a plus, but not required.

What Success Looks Like

Success isn't measured by the number of roadmaps created or projects launched.
You will help identify high-value opportunities before they become formal programs
, determine the right technology direction, influence investment and architecture decisions, help stand up the right initiatives, and stay connected through adoption and measurable business value.

We are looking for someone who naturally asks:

What problem are we actually solving?
What should the technology landscape look like three to five years from now?
What should we build, buy, integrate, pilot, scale, or stop? And how will we know it actually created value?

jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

About The IRC

The International Rescue Committee helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC works with people forced to flee from war, conflict and disaster and the host communities that support them, as well as with those who remain within their homes and communities. At work today in over 40 countries and 26 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure.

The IT department provides end-to-end solutions for the organization including application development & integration, system deployment, quality assurance & testing, and overall Project Management in an effort to help the organization build and implement the best solutions for its business needs.

The Opportunity

Every donation processed, every campaign that lands, every supporter who stays engaged — that's the technology you'll help build and deliver.

As IT Program Manager
, you'll manage the digital platforms behind one of the world's leading humanitarian organizations, directly enabling the fundraising that funds life-saving programs for displaced communities across the globe. This is a high-impact, fast-paced role at the intersection of technology delivery, stakeholder engagement, and mission-driven purpose.

Why Join Us?

Real-world impact — your work directly supports humanitarian programs serving millions of people in crisis.
Breadth and ownership — lead a complex, multi-platform portfolio with genuine strategic influence from day one.
Collaborative culture — work alongside Product Managers, Data Engineers, Business Analysts, and business stakeholders in a distributed, multicultural team that's deeply committed to its mission.
Modern delivery — Agile/Scrum at the core, with room to shape how the team works.
Remote-first flexibility — work from anywhere in the US as part of a truly global organization.

What You'll Do

Drive end-to-end program delivery

Develop and maintain detailed project plans, work breakdown structures, and product backlogs, ensuring delivery against time, budget, and quality targets.

Champion Agile ways of working

Manage budgets and vendors

jobs.description:
**Salary Grade**
----------------

  

Case Western Reserve University is committed to providing a transparent estimate of the salary range available for this position at the time of its posting. The salary range is between $49,257 and $62,311, depending on qualifications, experience, department budgets, and industry data.


Employees receive more than just a paycheck. University employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare, retirement plans, tuition assistance, paid time off, and a winter recess.


**Job Description**
-------------------

  

POSITION OBJECTIVE


Our research in Alzheimer's disease aims to identify genetic factors associated with dementia, specifically Alzheimer's type. We are focused on increasing the representation of our study population by enrolling individuals from various ancestries. Through this, we seek to better understand the genetic underpinnings of memory loss and dementia. By collecting comprehensive data and biological samples, we will conduct genetic studies to identify potential genetic markers for dementia. The Program Manager will play a key role in managing these efforts, including participant recruitment, enrollment, and data oversight, while collaborating with study sites to ensure the success of recruitment and data collection initiatives. This is a full\-time, 1 year term position.

  

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS


* Identify and enroll eligible individuals and meet enrollment goals. Cultivate relationships with potential study participants; providing education, building trust and promoting interest in study activities. Work within human research protection processes: create and maintain appropriate protocol documents, confidentially and sensitively obtain and review family and medical histories and perform study specific interviews, instruments, and exams and identify, obtain and review appropriate medical records. Draw blood for genetic studies (training can be provided on the job). Prepare detailed participant exam reports for adjudication. Oversee and maintain complete research files and comprehensive databases including: consent forms, demographics, family and medical history forms and all other study specific forms and data. Document and maintain records to show effort that may not be reflected in enrollment numbers; events attended, sign\-ups, declines, phone calls, messages left, etc. Ensure compliance with IRB approved protocols and maintain data integrity. (70%)


* Collaborate with study leadership to create strategic approaches to identify and engage community and clinic partnerships. Build community partnerships through effective outreach efforts. Develop and implement community recruitment strategy and methods. Design and manage community events; reach out to various groups including but not limited to the Alzheimer's association, churches, community senior centers, social groups and caregiver support groups. Maintain open communication with physicians and office staff participating in the studies in the community. Working closely with the research staff, monitor and oversee research activities for the ascertainment, recruitment and enrollment of study participants for the DAWN study and ensure timelines and goals are met. Evaluate outreach efforts, identify areas for improvement, advise leadership of alternative methods/efforts, and implement adjustments. (10%)


* Facilitate communication and provide regular research updates for meetings. Work with the team to prepare a yearly participant newsletter. Participate in research group meetings locally and with the national network and communicate with the Research Project Director and Principal Investigators to ensure that work on the studies is being performed as needed and expected. Attend regular meetings locally and nationally with the principal investigators/coordinators and collaborators. Maintain open communication/collaboration between departments within and outside of institution. (10%)


* Provide training and instruction regarding enrollment and data entry procedures for others working on the study. (7%)

Company Description

Matrixport-NY is a technology-driven financial services organization focused on building secure, scalable, and innovative digital asset solutions. The company leverages advanced information technology and data-driven decision-making to support a broad range of institutional and enterprise clients. Matrixport-NY emphasizes rigorous risk management, regulatory awareness, and operational excellence in all technology initiatives. Team members work in a collaborative, high-performance environment that values transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement. The organization offers opportunities to shape modern financial technology infrastructure and contribute to long-term strategic growth.

Role Description

The Vice President of Technology is a full-time, remote leadership role responsible for defining and executing the company’s technology vision and strategy. This role oversees the design, implementation, and maintenance of core platforms, infrastructure, and applications supporting digital asset and financial services operations. Day-to-day responsibilities include leading technology teams, prioritizing and managing projects, aligning IT initiatives with business goals, and establishing best practices for security, reliability, and scalability. The Vice President of Technology collaborates closely with executive leadership, product, operations, and compliance teams to ensure technology roadmaps support regulatory requirements and organizational growth. jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is responsible for leading the company’s overall technology strategy, infrastructure, product development, cybersecurity, and technical operations. The CTO will align technology initiatives with business objectives, drive innovation, build high\-performing engineering teams, and ensure the company maintains scalable, secure, and reliable technology systems.

**Key Responsibilities**

\* Develop and execute the company’s long\-term technology strategy and roadmap.

\* Lead technology, engineering, software development, IT, data, and cybersecurity functions.

\* Translate business goals into effective technology solutions and initiatives.

\* Oversee the design, development, deployment, and maintenance of software products and platforms.

\* Establish scalable technology architecture and infrastructure.

\* Ensure systems are secure, reliable, high\-performing, and cost\-effective.

\* Lead digital transformation and adoption of emerging technologies, including AI and automation.

\* Establish technology standards, development processes, and best practices.

\* Manage technology budgets, vendors, technology investments, and resource allocation.

\* Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain senior technical talent.

\* Work closely with the CEO, COO, CFO, CPO, and other executives on strategic initiatives.

\* Identify and manage technology risks, cybersecurity threats, and compliance requirements.

\* Establish KPIs and performance metrics for technology teams and initiatives.

\* Evaluate new technologies, platforms, tools, and strategic partnerships.

\* Ensure business continuity, disaster recovery, data protection, and system availability.

\* Communicate complex technical concepts and technology strategy to executive leadership and stakeholders.

**Required Qualifications**

\* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.

\* Master’s degree or MBA is preferred.

\* \*10\+ years of experience\* in technology, software engineering, IT, or a related field.

\* \*5\+ years of leadership/management experience\*, preferably at a senior or executive level.

\* Proven experience developing and executing technology strategies.

\* Experience leading engineering or technology organizations.

\* Strong understanding of cloud computing, software architecture, cybersecurity, databases, APIs, and modern development practices.

\* Experience managing technology budgets and large\-scale projects.

\* Strong knowledge of Agile, DevOps, CI/CD, and software development lifecycle practices.

**Preferred Skills**

\* Strategic leadership and business acumen

\* Software and systems architecture

\* Cloud platforms and infrastructure

\* Artificial intelligence and machine learning

\* Cybersecurity and risk management

\* Data analytics and technology governance

\* Product development

\* Digital transformation

\* Vendor and partner management

\* Budget and resource management

\* Executive communication and presentation

\* Change management

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**

\* Technology uptime and system reliability

\* Product development and delivery timelines

\* Technology cost efficiency

\* Cybersecurity and compliance performance

\* Engineering productivity

\* Product quality and customer experience

\* Successful implementation of technology roadmap

\* Employee retention and development within technology teams

\* Innovation and adoption of strategic technologies

Join us as our Chief Technology Officer to lead transformative projects that redefine our technological capabilities! We value energetic leaders who are passionate about shaping the future through innovative solutions while ensuring security integrity across all platforms. This is your chance to influence strategic decisions at the highest level—driving growth through cutting\-edge technology!

Work Location: Remote
